To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have shown a very fast heterogeneous electron transfer between cyctochrome P450(cam) and an electrode surface modified with sodium montomorillonite.
the heterogeneous electron transfer between P450(cam) and an electrode is fast enough to be used as a model for the natural electron transport from putidaredexin.

a very fast electron transfer between P450(cam) and a glassy carbon surface modified with clay colloidal particles is demonstrated and that the formal potential of P450(cam), adsorbed on such a surface, is positively shifted by 160 mV compared to P450(cam) dissolved in solution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new approach for electrochemical investigation of the redox reactions of cytochromes and other metalloproteins in the absence of substrates.
the development of a new type of electrode for electroenzymology.
the design of an artificial redox-active surface that allows for fast heterogeneous electron transfer to a protein.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the clay colloids are not directly involved in the electron transfer process.
the electron transfer between the electrode and the adsorbed P45O(cam) occurs via the clay colloids.
the clay colloids do not affect the redox potential of the heme iron in the P450(cam) but rather facilitate the electron transfer between the protein and the electrode.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated that the clay colloids are suitable for the preparation of modified electrodes for the electrochemical study of proteins.
we have developed an efficient method for electrochemical studies of cytochromes P450, and in particular, for the investigation of their electron transfer reactions.
the clay colloidal particle can act as a mediator for the electron transfer between P450(cam) and the glassy carbon electrode.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the clay colloids may be used for the immobilization of redox enzymes on electrodes.
the clay-modified glassy carbon electrode can be used for electrochemical studies of the redox behavior of proteins in solution and on the surface of electrode.
the clay-bridged electron-transfer reaction of cytochrome P(450)(cam) is very fast and can be used for the development of new electrochemical biosensors for the detection of toxic compounds.
